Ladybird Nursery (2-3 year olds.)
Sessions are as follows:
Children are required to attend for a minimum of two regular 3 hour sessions a week.

Option One: Monday and Tuesday 8.45am - 3pm, and Wednesday 8.45am - 11.45 (15 hours universal funding)
Option Two: Wednesday 12 noon - 3pm, Thursdays and Friday 8.45am-11.45am (15 hours universal funding)
Option Three: Full time, ie Monday to Friday 8.45-3pm (15 hours universal funding and 15+ hours Working Parent Entitlement)

pageCache.pageTitle: ST JUDE'S CHURCH OF ENGLAND SCHOOLS FEDERATION - Our Governors
pageCache.text:
Our Governors
Governors can be contacted through the school office or by emailing governors@stjudes.surrey.sch.uk. Emails will be considered in a timely and professional manner.
Please see the links below for further Governor Information.
Meet our Governors
Juan Pemberton (Foundation Governor) CHAIR
Juan's experience encompasses specialist and generalist management skills in a number of commercial and HR roles. As Deputy Group HR Director of Direct Line Insurance Group, Juan was part of the leadership team that floated the company on the London Stock Exchange in 2012. A two-year Sabbatical followed, during which extensive travel to Africa, Asia and Australia were highlights.
Juan's roots are in the Isle of Man (hence his name 'Jew-un' ) albeit he now lives in Windsor. His most recent business role was as the HR Director of Barclays Retail Bank based in Canary Wharf, London.
Dan Parsonage (Staff Governor) SAFEGUARDING
I’m employed as Technical Operations Manager at Royal Holloway University of London. At RHUL I'm responsible for Health and Safety which ranges from day to day H&S through to laboratory process and plant areas, along with planning and implementing a Covid-19 compliant campus for teaching and research. I sit on various senior committees within RHUL, one being for college capital investment appraisal.
I have always worked in higher education in a science setting including research and teaching and I feel with my experiences I can offer support to the school as a parent governor. I have two children, one in year 4, Maxime, and then Oscar in year 7. I feel it is time to give something back to the community and school.
Vicki Chiverton (Headteacher)
Vicki starting teaching in 1991 and has previously worked in schools in Berkshire and Buckinghamshire. Having lived in Englefield Green and surrounding area for quite some time, Vicki understands the diverse needs of the village and its children. After ten years as a deputy head and keen to lead a school of such high regard, she took up her first headship at St Jude’s in April 2008 and loves the school so much that she is still here!
Pru Ashplant (Associate Member)
Pru started teaching in 2001 in Somerset and moved to St Jude’s in 2005. She was appointed Deputy Head in 2009, initially of the junior school but she now works across both schools and thoroughly enjoys working alongside her colleagues and the children of all ages. Pru's key responsibility is the quality of teaching and learning.
Vaughan Pryce-Jenkins (Parent Governor)
I am a parent of children at all stages of St Jude’s schools (Junior, Infants, Pre-school) and I am excited at the opportunity to listen, learn and support the school as a parent governor.
I am a civil engineer, working on the design of offshore wind farms. I lead a team of fantastic, diverse engineers and work on a number of complex projects all over the world, which require management, leadership, problem-solving and communication skills. Through work, I have also been an active STEM ambassador in schools.
Canon Judith Allford (Ex-officio)
Canon Judith Allford was named as vicar at St Jude's Church in 2019. As our St Jude's Schools are church schools, with extremely close links to St Jude's Church, this means we are delighted to welcome Judith, as ex-officio, to the governing body. Judith will be vital in maintaining the school's Christian values.
Revd Jeremy Brown (Ex-officio)
Rev Jeremy Brown is one of the foundation (church appointed governors) from Christ Church Virginia Water. He is the children and families pastor at Christ Church. He, along with Judith, take Monday morning assemblies at the school.
Jeremy is married to Clair, and they have 3 children: Grace and Samuel are at Magna Carta and Daniel attends Manor Mead Virginia Water. He enjoys football and supports Aston Villa!
Helen McKee (Foundation Governor)
Helen has a long-standing interest in education, having taught at university level since the 1990s; she also ran a Sunday school for several years. Her two children are both now at secondary school but both attended St Jude’s Infant and Junior schools. Helen is also on the Admissions Committee and is SEND governor.
Carlos Pittol (Foundation Governor) VICE CHAIR
Carlos has been a governor since 2009, first at Englefield Green Infant School and then at St Jude's Junior School and is now on the Federated governing body of St Jude's Schools. He has two daughters; both of whom attended St Jude's Schools. Carlos was a research chemist and now works in venture capital finance and biotechnology. He has a broad knowledge of and a keen interest in education, especially maths and science.
Sam Jenkins (Foundation Governor)
Sam Jenkins joins the Governing Body at St Jude's with experience across the education, civic and third sectors. In May 2022 he was elected to represent Egham as a Runnymede Borough Councillor. His main policy interests are climate change, sustainability and provision for children and young people. Sam also sits on a number of other governing committees within the local community, including Runnymede Access Liaison Group, which supports and advocates for those with physical and hidden disabilities.
Danail Popov (Associate member)
I am excited to be join the Governing Body as an Associate Member. Both my daughters were pupils at the Infant and Junior schools. I have lived in the local area for over 20 years, having previously been a student at Royal Holloway University where I read Economics. I have been working as a professional economist in London for almost 20 years. My day job involves analysis and problem solving which regularly draws on financial data. I look forward to supporting the school by utilising my expertise.
Will Hall (Associate Member)
Will is a civil servant working on major events within the Cabinet Office. He has experience leading teams that have helped respond to most of the major events and incidents that have impacted the UK over the last few years.
Prior to this, Will was an officer within the British Army, training and leading soldiers in various locations, including two tours of Afghanistan. He is a generalist who hopes to bring a range of leadership and project management skills to help support the St. Jude's Federation. As a new governor, he is keen to learn from the team and support wherever he can.
Will lives in Egham with his wife Emma, their daughter Olivia, who is a pupil thriving at the infant school, their toddler son Max and their dog Hector!

pageCache.pageTitle: ST JUDE'S CHURCH OF ENGLAND SCHOOLS FEDERATION - SEND
pageCache.text:
SEND
St Jude’s C of E Schools Federation strongly believes that, as stated in the Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Code of Practice (2015), ‘all pupils and young people are entitled to an education that enables them to make progress so that they: achieve their best, become confident individuals living fulfilling lives and make a successful transition into adulthood.’
We respect the unique contribution which every individual makes to the community and seek to embrace the highest possible academic aspirations for each pupil, as well as accepting individual differences in ability, aptitude and level of skills. At St Jude’s C of E Schools Federation, every teacher is a teacher of every pupil, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
Mrs Stanton and Mrs Hutchinson are our SENDCOs (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Coordinators). If you have any queries regarding SEND, please contact them via the office at school@stjudes.surrey.sch.uk.
For more information on how we support pupils with SEND, please see the documents below.
Please also find below a link to information regarding Ordinary Available Provision for both schools and parents.

pageCache.pageTitle: ST JUDE'S CHURCH OF ENGLAND SCHOOLS FEDERATION - Curriculum Information
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Information
Education at St Jude’s respects and celebrates differences: inspired by the example of St Jude, our interactions are anchored in hope, compassion, perseverance, responsibility, respect and forgiveness. We appreciate God-given talent and potential and emphasise the personal worth and progress of each pupil. We prepare pupils for the next stage in their journey of life - educational, emotional and spiritual.
St Jude’s curriculum is broad, balanced and accessible to all learners. We recognise the importance of a strong foundation in English and maths, coupled with building skills in other curriculum areas, enabling pupils to apply their acquired knowledge to solving problems. Literature is carefully selected to develop reading skills and vocabulary, enrich the wider curriculum and to promote the sheer love of reading. By interweaving, where appropriate, discrete subjects through cross curricular topics, pupils are able to make meaningful and memorable links which deepen their learning.
Education at St Jude’s is engaging and offers relevant experiences. We believe that hard work leads to achievement and a greater sense of self-worth, fostering resilience and the courage to take risk. Enjoyment and high expectations are fundamental to developing good learning behaviours which are further developed through strong partnerships with parents.
With excellence in education at the core of our purpose, our reflective, dedicated team continually strives to ensure that every child is happy, well cared for and feels valued for their uniqueness.
Within the infant school, we have one two nurseries, a Reception class, a Year 1 class and a Year 2 class. At the junior school, we have one Year 3 class, two Year 4 classes, one Year 5 class and two Year 6 classes. Prior to this school year (2026-27) we have had mixed-aged classes at both the infant and junior schools and are now reverting to single-aged classes, so the planning for teaching will reflect this change.

pageCache.pageTitle: ST JUDE'S CHURCH OF ENGLAND SCHOOLS FEDERATION - Nurseries
pageCache.text:
Nurseries
NURSERY PROVISION IS SITUATED AT THE INFANT SCHOOL ON BARLEY MOW ROAD.
Ladybird Nursery provides flexible care for 2-3 year olds.
Sessions are as follows:
Ladybird Nursery has a bright and airy inside area as well as a large and well-resourced outdoor area. Collectively, this provides a wide range of open-ended resources and activities, including construction, mark making, creative activities, water, sand, reading area, play dough, music, mud kitchen, small world and more!
Our learning environment is carefully designed to allow children to access resources independently, encouraging children to follow their own interests.
Butterfly Nursery provides flexible care for 3-4 year olds.
Children attend either half or full-time as follows:
Part-time Monday to Wednesday
Part-Time Wednesday to Friday
Full-time Monday to Friday
A typical day in Butterfly class includes two short periods of class ‘carpet time’ activities, such as stories, music, phonics, numeracy or circle time, together with lots and lots of child-led play. We play both indoors and outside every day. The Butterfly staff team follow the children’s play interests to support their learning and development within this fun-filled and active environment.
Monday 8.45am – 3.00pm
Tuesday 8:45am – 3.00pm
Wednesday 8.45am – 11.45am
Wednesday 12.00 noon – 3.00pm
Thursday 8.45am – 3.00pm
Friday 8.45am – 3.00pm
Monday to Friday 8.45am – 3.00pm

pageCache.text:
30 Hours Entitlement
We accept FEET funding and Working Parent Funding. For non-funded children sessions will be charged at market rates - see Charging and Remissions Policy.
Children attending full-time may be entitled to 30 free hours through the 15 hours universal funding and 15+ hours Working Parent Entitlement.
For further information on checking your eligibility for the 30 hours childcare entitlement please visit:
https://www.surreycc.gov.uk/schools-and-learning/childcare-professionals/providing-free-early-education/providing-plus-15-hours-of-free-childcare.
